chunks: As if I see (him), he (the Enjoiner of Evil) [2] is shouting in Syria (ash-Shām) and is extending his banners to the outskirts of Kūfah. He is bent towards it like the biting of the she-camel. He has covered the ground with heads. His mouth is wide open and (the trampling of) his footsteps on the ground have become heavy. His advance is broad and his attacks are severe.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor 'biting of the she-camel' in this sermon?
ai.summary: This passage from the 'Foretelling events' chapter of Nahj al-Balagha is widely interpreted by Shia scholars as a vivid description of the Umayyad conquest, specifically referencing the campaigns of Mu'awiya or the expansion into Kufa. The imagery of 'striking like a camel' and 'scattering heads' underscores the brutal consolidation of power and the heavy toll on the people of Kufa, reflecting the historical tension between the Syrian caliphate and the Iraqi center. It serves as a prophetic narrative linking political dominance with spiritual and physical subjugation.
